items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-23
items.q: Was it near Jack Sheen's place? Yeah, there in Sue's Band. Was it near Jack Sheen's up around there? Yeah.

ctx.x: Yeah. And then when he brought that long-necked band in there, he was a band. He had two people. He had one on them, you know. Mm-hmm. He saw that he was making of a outstanding band. They let him, you know, use him, you know, demonstrate. Man, what you got there, man? I don't know, but I'm going to try it out tonight. I said, well, you got the other guitar? Oh, yeah, I got it. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . you know, Renee was waking up at the…

Why, that's it. Yeah, I did see one one time. I was looking for Rene, and I went to this Cadillac Club down on St. Claude, and they had one there, you know. But I never paid attention to it, you know. I'd rather listen to the music and find the girls later.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Was it near Jack Sheen's place? ... [INTERVIEWEE] Near the suburban gardens, right there?

ctx.x: I didn't wake there for two years. And then, we got to the poppy, you know, and come and sign us at the Astor, you know? Rene was waking at the Astor until, you know, Sunday night until 12 o'clock. Then, we take over at 12.30, you know, after our dance, make $78. Mm-hmm. Got poppy there, and he had a place out there in Sue's Bay. Oh, Ridley was waking up there. Ridley and Schatz, Libby Ridley. Libby was playing drum, yes.
Was it near Jack Sheen's place? Yeah, at that Sue's Bay. Yeah, was it near Jack Sheen's up around there? Yeah.
Near the suburban gardens, right there? Yeah, on the other side of the suburban gardens. Right there, huh?
